_comment: A response whose `data` rows are NOT application log events.
The behaviour this pins: a row missing `message`, `level` or `source`, or
carrying a timestamp that is not a time, is dropped rather than coerced.
Inventing a missing `level` would produce an event that looks real and that
no log ever emitted it — which is the failure mode the whole parser exists to
prevent. Three unusable rows, so a parser that returned them would report 3
Row 3 is the subtle one: it has all three required fields, and only the
timestamp is unusable. Accepting it would put NaN into `LogEvent.timestamp`,
which makes every `--since` comparison false — so the event would survive the
provider filter and then be dropped by the local predicate for the wrong
reason, or render as `NaN` in the human output.
`rows_read: 0` alongside them is the other thing worth pinning: the provider can
report having read nothing while rows are present, so `rows_read` is reported
rather than used to decide whether a result is empty.

data.message: has a message but no level and no source
level, message and source, but an unparseable timestamp
